title: Dietary supplementation with a wild green oat extract (Avena sativa L.) to improve wellness and wellbeing during smoking reduction or cessation: a randomized double-blind controlled study.
disposition: Wild green-oat extract RCT in smokers measured actigraphic wake after sleep onset. Existing 0174 assessment notes the exposure and outcome mismatch.

title: Granola consumption with multiple prebiotics in Japanese participants increases Bifidobacterium abundance and improves stress and subjective sleepiness.
disposition: Original main report. One-arm granola and milk intervention lowered self-reported insomnia scores from baseline. EEG outcomes were inconclusive and the rolled-oat content is unverified.

title: Effectiveness of personalized granola tailored to the gut microbiota for improving gut environment and mood states.
disposition: Original main report. A distinct uncontrolled personalized granola study found inconclusive overall insomnia scores. Exact supplemental recipe remains unverified.

title: Bridging Science and Lifestyle: A Feasibility Study for Developing a Novel Functional Food to Support Well-being
disposition: Primary survey and later publication DOI 10.3390/nutraceuticals5020010 describe food-format preferences, including granola, without an assigned oat exposure or a sleep intervention.

title: A Preliminary Study of the Effects of SurAsleep on Relieving Symptoms of Sleep Disorders.
disposition: Original Xie report assesses an oat-straw, melatonin, valerian and mineral mixture. Final sleep-quality score favors the combination. Oats were never isolated.

title: Food Quality Is Associated With Depression, Anxiety, and Stress Among Recovered COVID-19 Patients: Finding From a Case-Control Study.
disposition: Primary full text https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11832289/ reports observational food quality score, ISI and PSQI in 246 recovered COVID cases and controls; pooled whole grains are a score component, with no isolated rolled oat intervention or Parkinson cohort. The abstract's named significant score associations concern depression, anxiety and stress; do not attribute them to insomnia.

title: Adherence to the nordic diet is associated with anxiety, stress, and depression in recovered COVID-19 patients, a case-control study.
disposition: Primary abstract https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38429766/ reports Nordic diet case-control study, 123 recovered COVID cases and 123 controls, likely same study family as 39968276 and 36369107; whole-grain correlations are with depression, anxiety and stress, whereas reported insomnia and sleep-quality correlation is for root vegetables. Full original https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10908094/ challenged; retain full-body depth open.

title: Physical activity, sugar-sweetened beverages, whole grain bread and insomnia among adolescents and psychological distress in adulthood: prospective data from the population-based HUNT study.
disposition: Primary abstract https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34724961/ is HUNT prospective study of 2230 adolescents; whole-grain bread and insomnia are separate adolescent predictors of adult psychological distress, not a bread intervention with insomnia outcome. No isolated rolled oats or Parkinson; PMC full body challenge encountered.

title: Adherence to dietary approaches to stop hypertension (DASH) diet in relation to psychological function in recovered COVID-19 patients: a case-control study.
disposition: Primary abstract https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36369107/ describes 123 recovered COVID cases and 123 controls, DASH score and ISI/PSQI; reported whole-grain association concerns depression, anxiety and stress, not established insomnia benefit. Likely same case-control family as 38429766 and 39968276; PMC https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9651111/ challenged and deeper body remains open.

title: High glycemic index and glycemic load diets as risk factors for insomnia: analyses from the Women's Health Initiative.
disposition: Original full text https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6997082/ observational WHI postmenopausal cohort: whole-grain intake predictor, self-reported insomnia outcome. Highest vs lowest quintile fully adjusted prevalent insomnia OR 0.93 (95% CI 0.88–0.98), n=77860; incident insomnia OR 1.00 (0.93–1.07), n=53069, 3-year follow-up. Broad whole-grain category, no isolated rolled oat or PD comparison; associations not causal.

title: Measures of Poor Sleep Quality Are Associated With Higher Energy Intake and Poor Diet Quality in a Diverse Sample of Women From the Go Red for Women Strategically Focused Research Network.
disposition: Primary abstract https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32063123/ cross-sectional women n=495: sleep-onset latency is predictor and whole-grain intake is dietary outcome; latency >60 vs <=15 minutes associated with less whole grain (beta -0.37, p=0.01). Greater ISI relates to energy, food weight and fats; abstract does not establish whole-grain effect on insomnia. PMC full body challenged.

title: Impact of a Nordic diet on psychological function in young students.
disposition: Primary abstract https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33076738/ cross-sectional 181 young female students; Nordic-diet adherence and ISI measured, significant reported cabbage/vegetable associations with stress, anxiety and quality of life, not a demonstrated whole-grain insomnia result. No separate rolled-oat or Parkinson exposure; primary full body unverified.
